item.title: Correct Two Names on a Museum Map
item.prompt_text: A museum map printed last month calls a room the East Study while the sign above its door says Map Room. The same map also labels a different room East Study, which is correct. Visitors have missed tours because some staff use the printed name in directions. Draft a public correction that distinguishes the two rooms, gives visitors an immediate way to check their destination, and explains how the museum will introduce the updated map without blaming staff.
item.target_grammar: Specific reference; concessive and relative clauses; future forms for publication changes.
item.target_structure: Name the old and current labels → give two location cues → explain the immediate workaround → state the change and timing.

checklist.point: Correct the two room names with clear identifying details.
Give a route or identifying detail visitors can act on immediately.
Explain how staff and visitors will be told about the replacement.
Use accountable wording without blaming individual staff.
